newsitem.title: USA: CBOT old crop soybeans jump on export inspections.
newsitem.headline: CBOT old crop soybeans jump on export inspections.

text.p: CBOT old crop May and July soybeans turned higher on fast dealings on USDA export inspections that came in above trade expectations, floor sources said.

USDA on Monday put weekly soybean export inspections at 18.9 million bushels, above expectations for nine million to 13 million bushels and well above the previous week's figure of 8.9 million bushels.

Floor sources said the strong weekly figure suggested prices had not risen enough to ration demand. Analysts and traders have said the combination of weekly exports and crush needs to fall below 30 million bushels per week to meet USDA's ending stocks projection of 125 million bushels.
The crush last week was at 25.6 million bushels.
At 1008 CDT, soybeans were 6-1/4 cents per bushel higher to six cents lower with May up 6-1/4 at $8.74 and new crop November down six at $6.92.
